symptom: `menu item 'A' (…, Icon: glyph 57388)` — a code the glyph font does not define — prints MDL078 as a warning, exec applies it, `mx check` reports 0 errors, and `mxbuild --target=deploy` exits 1 with System.InvalidOperationException 'Sequence contains no matching element' at GlyphFont.GetClass, naming a layout, and writes NO --write-errors file (a CE error exits 3 and writes one), so a build gate has nothing to report
cause: MDL078 was deliberately a warning: the glyph table was treated as a snapshot of a Mendix asset that might grow, so refusing was judged worse than letting the build fail
insight: The snapshot risk was measurable and nobody had measured it: mxbuild bundles its own modeler/glyphicons-halflings-regular.ttf, byte-identical (sha256 e3950440…57456) in 9.24, 10.12, 11.6.6 and 11.15.0, and its format-4 cmap private-use range is exactly the 247 codes in glyphIcons. A hedge against a change that has not happened in four major versions is not worth a crash with no error file. The control for 'no error file' is the same build with a real CE error: exit 3 and a populated errors JSON. A glyph has no name, so 'check the icon name' became naming the defined codes either side of the bad one (57385 play-circle / 57392 repeat for 57388). Every carrier (nav menu, menu document, page/snippet/layout widget) goes through iconRefsInStatement, so one severity change covers all of them; ALTER PAGE SET has no glyph spelling
